title: Supersymmetry and Entanglement in the Generalized Dirac Oscillator
authors: H. P. Laba, V. M. Tkachuk
abstract: The supersymmetric properties of the generalized Dirac oscillator allow us to determine the entanglement entropy between the spin and the continuous variable in a purely algebraic manner. The entanglement has a relativistic origin and disappears in the nonrelativistic limit. The entanglement entropy attains its maximal value in the limit of infinite energy.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the entanglement between spin and continuous variables in the generalized Dirac oscillator using supersymmetric techniques. It shows that the calculated entanglement entropy is zero for the ground state but grows with energy, confirming that this correlation is fundamentally relativistic. The findings highlight how underlying symmetries govern quantum information properties in relativistic field models.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between supersymmetry (SUSY) properties and quantum entanglement within generalized Dirac oscillator systems.
main_result: The entanglement entropy is found to be zero for the ground state but increases with energy, reaching a maximum value in the infinite energy limit. Crucially, this entanglement has a purely relativistic origin, vanishing in the nonrelativistic limit.
method: The analysis uses SUSY transformations to decouple the system into components ($	ilde{\phi}, 	ilde{\chi}$) and calculates the entanglement entropy by finding the eigenvalues of the reduced density matrix traced over continuous variables.
model_or_system: The model is a (1+1)-dimensional generalized Dirac oscillator, which is a relativistic quantum mechanical system whose Hamiltonian incorporates SUSY structure. The analysis involves solving coupled differential equations derived from the eigenvalue problem.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy ($S$), overlap integral ($Z$), and the energy eigenvalues ($E$).

main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the existence of a supersymmetric structure ($\hat{B}, \hat{B}^+$) to relate the system's components.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the SUSY framework for the generalized Dirac oscillator, then parameterizes the state vector using SUSY partners. It proceeds to calculate the entanglement entropy based on these components and analyzes its dependence on energy and symmetry properties.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how fundamental symmetries (SUSY) can dictate non-trivial quantum correlations (entanglement) in relativistic models, offering insights applicable to structured quantum systems beyond standard qubit architectures.
